claims.text: A hybrid approach combining TOR-TILD with machine-learning interatomic potentials can improve thermodynamic-property determination for multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperatures.
The proposed target is a multicomponent high-entropy material in a solid or fluid state near the solid-to-fluid transition.
The intervention is implementation of a hybrid TOR-TILD and machine-learning interatomic-potential approach.
High-entropy alloys present a large compositional space.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can efficiently sample the compositional space of multicomponent high-entropy materials.
TOR-TILD supplies accurate values for critical thermodynamic properties.
The hybrid method can treat both solid and dense-fluid phases around the transition.
The hybrid method can retain ab initio-level accuracy.

Interatomic-potential simulations of a quinary Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni alloy can quantitatively agree with first-principles calculations and experiments for selected structural, stability, ordering, and mechanical properties.
The hybrid method will improve the accuracy of transition-temperature determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The hybrid method will improve the accuracy of fusion-enthalpy and fusion-entropy determination relative to existing methods.
The hybrid method will improve the accuracy of transition volume-change determination relative to existing methods.
The hybrid method will improve the accuracy of dense-fluid heat-capacity determination relative to existing methods.
The hybrid method will be more computationally efficient than existing DFT free-energy and TOR-TILD methods.
Existing TOR-TILD baseline results concern elemental and binary systems.
The approach is applicable only over compositions and temperatures for which it can be trained and validated.
Transferability of interatomic potentials across diverse high-entropy-alloy compositions is uncertain.
TOR-TILD calculations may incur errors for complex multicomponent systems.
